svg.title: Which nursing actions are required for a patient receiving TPN through a central line? Select all that apply.
svg.desc: TPN IS ICU-LEVEL THERAPY THAT GOES STRAIGHT INTO THE BLOODSTREAM — every carb, electrolyte, vitamin, and gram of protein is systemic, so it demands a second-nurse bag verification, glucose monitoring, daily weights, and I&O. Hanging the wrong bag is a med error, which is exactly why a second nurse verifies it; each bag is mixed in pharmacy with your patient's name on it. Glucose checks continue for the duration of therapy because carbs are going directly into the blood and the patient can swing hyperglycemic or hypoglycemic at any point. Be the nurse who is fanatical about scrubbing that port every single time — a central line infection is preventable, and sepsis from a dirty port can kill your patient.
